claim: In the November 1972 election Richard Nixon defeated Democrat George McGovern in a landslide: 60.7% of the popular vote to 37.5%, carrying 49 states and 520 electoral votes to McGovern's 17 (McGovern won only Massachusetts and the District of Columbia). The ~18 million-vote margin was the largest raw popular-vote margin in U.S. history to that point. The reel's claim that it was the "biggest landslide ever" is the strongest version: by other measures Nixon's win was not the single largest — Lyndon Johnson took a higher popular-vote share in 1964 (61.1%) and Ronald Reagan won more electoral votes in 1984 (525).

sources.label: 1972 United States presidential election — popular vote, states, and electoral count.
sources.quote: Nixon won the election in a landslide victory, taking 60.7% of the popular vote, carrying 49 states and becoming the first Republican to sweep the South, whereas McGovern took just 37.5% of the popular vote.

notes: Group A spine with a Group B superlative. The reel (Rogan relaying Tucker Carlson on American Alchemy, DRsrlmcEhzu) frames the landslide to set up 'why would he break into the DNC if he was winning anyway' — the paranoia premise. 'Biggest ever' is defensible by raw-vote margin, not by EV (Reagan 1984) or popular-vote % (LBJ 1964).
